title: Document direction separates a label reference from a repeated caption
summary: GDT790 observes opposite textual directions: otedy is a visible label followed by a prose-record opener, while okal occurs in prose before its panel label. Test whether direction predicts reference versus learned-name use without using spatial proximity as semantic evidence.

design.mechanism: A complete form's document-order relation between label and prose occurrence distinguishes a textual reference/caption from a learned name reused as a label.
design.unit: exact multi-character label/prose bridges with independently recorded panel, paragraph record, and document order
design.contrast: label-to-prose reference versus prose-to-label repeated caption/name
design.prediction: Across held cross-panel bridges, label-first forms should behave as explicit prose references, while prose-first forms should recur as names or captions that can be introduced before their label; the direction should remain after matching panel and record role.
design.falsifier: When independent textual-role coding shows no stable relation between document direction and reference/name behavior across held bridges, the direction-based construction fails.
design.scope_note: This does not infer a physical owner, object name, or free component meaning from proximity. It is a source-starting document-order hypothesis with semantic endpoint availability unknown.
design.related: Near GDT790/GDT792 label-prose coverage and GDT798 text-host comparisons, but targets document-direction asymmetry rather than closed panel-owner, slot, or immediate-proximity routes.
design.countermodel: Editorial ordering or paragraph layout can place labels before or after prose without changing their semantic role; a repeated caption can occur in either direction.

source_evidence.quote:
## The exact bridges that matter

Four multi-character label forms recur exactly in prose, producing nine usable
occurrence edges:

| Label form | Picture owner | Prose bridge | Current use |
|---|---|---|---|
| `otedy` | f77r upper arch, inner port 2 | f77r P2 opener plus four f82r/f83r occurrences | same-page back-reference candidate; cross-page name/formula |
| `okal` | f82r lower pool, upper station 2 | f82r P1 and P2 | forward/shared-station reference candidate |
| `otchdy` | f77r middle west figure-zone | f83r Q1 opener | recurring name/formula at an embedded record head |
| `olaiin` | f82r lower pool, figure 6 | f77r P3 | recurring label/name form |

The remaining edge is the one-character token `o` from f77r.50; it is retained
for completeness and excluded as an anchor.

The useful asymmetry is new. `otedy` is first a visible upper-arch label and
then exactly the first token of f77r P2. `okal` runs in the opposite document
direction: it occurs in two earlier prose records before appearing as a lower
pool label. Labels can therefore behave as references or learned names, not
only as captions sitting next to their paragraph.

design.principal_risk: Document direction may be an artifact of layout or editorial ordering, and the current panel/paragraph labels are not independent semantic gold.

design_stop_notes: A name can function as a reference in either document direction; reference and learned-name use are not exclusive by order alone.
Document order is not independently proven to be the authorial reading order.
Layout/editorial order can produce the observed asymmetry without semantic direction.
